author: Warren Wurzer, Limitless Solutions Consulting
description: Canonical variable definitions for the Wurzer Meta-Adjacency Framework. All variables normalized to 0.0–1.0. Positive variables increase adjacency score. Negative variables decrease adjacency score.

positive_variables.name: capability_distance
positive_variables.note: Inverted during scoring: closer capabilities = higher score
positive_variables.definition: How close the target opportunity is to the company's existing capabilities. Higher values indicate closer alignment and less adaptation required.

interpretation.0.8–1.0: Direct extension of current capabilities — minimal adaptation required
interpretation.0.6–0.79: Strong capability overlap — minor gaps to fill
interpretation.0.2–0.39: Weak overlap — significant new capability build needed

positive_variables.name: customer_overlap
positive_variables.definition: Degree of overlap between current customers and the customers of the adjacent opportunity. Higher values mean the same buyers purchase both offerings.

interpretation.0.8–1.0: Same customer base — near-zero acquisition cost for adjacency
interpretation.0.6–0.79: Strong overlap — majority of target customers already engaged
interpretation.0.4–0.59: Partial overlap — mixed new and existing customers
interpretation.0.2–0.39: Low overlap — primarily new customer acquisition required

positive_variables.name: asset_reusability
positive_variables.definition: Extent to which existing assets — relationships, infrastructure, knowledge, brand, geography, technology — can be redeployed into the new opportunity.

interpretation.0.8–1.0: High leverage of existing assets — minimal new investment required
interpretation.0.6–0.79: Strong asset reuse — some supplemental investment needed
interpretation.0.4–0.59: Some assets transferable — moderate investment required
interpretation.0.2–0.39: Limited asset reuse — significant new asset build
interpretation.0.0–0.19: No asset reuse possible — full greenfield investment

positive_variables.name: market_proximity
positive_variables.definition: Closeness of the adjacent market in terms of industry, channel, regulatory environment, or geography.

interpretation.0.8–1.0: Directly neighboring market — same regulatory environment, channels, buyers
interpretation.0.6–0.79: Adjacent but distinct — familiar dynamics with some new elements
interpretation.0.4–0.59: Related market — meaningful differences requiring adaptation
interpretation.0.2–0.39: Distant market — significant new knowledge required
interpretation.0.0–0.19: Entirely new market — no meaningful proximity

positive_variables.name: synergy_potential
positive_variables.definition: How much the new opportunity strengthens the core business, or is strengthened by it, through shared assets, brand, operations, or knowledge.

interpretation.0.8–1.0: High synergy — adjacency and core reinforce each other strongly
interpretation.0.6–0.79: Good synergy — clear operational and commercial leverage
interpretation.0.4–0.59: Some synergy — limited but real cross-benefit

positive_variables.name: scalability_index
positive_variables.definition: How well the opportunity scales once validated, without proportional increases in cost or complexity.

interpretation.0.8–1.0: High scalability — recurring revenue, automation potential, low incremental cost
interpretation.0.6–0.79: Good scalability — grows well with moderate operational lift
interpretation.0.2–0.39: Low scalability — labor-intensive or capital-constrained growth
interpretation.0.0–0.19: Negligible scalability — one-off or highly constrained

positive_variables.name: strategic_optionality
positive_variables.definition: How many future strategic moves this opportunity unlocks. High optionality means entering this adjacency opens further adjacencies.

interpretation.0.8–1.0: Platform-level optionality — unlocks multiple future expansion paths
interpretation.0.6–0.79: Strong optionality — opens 2–3 meaningful future paths

negative_variables.name: friction_score
negative_variables.definition: Regulatory, operational, competitive, and workflow friction associated with entering the opportunity. Higher values indicate more friction and reduce the adjacency score.

interpretation.0.0–0.19: Near-zero friction — open market, light regulation, low competition
interpretation.0.4–0.59: Moderate friction — real but surmountable barriers
interpretation.0.6–0.79: High friction — significant barriers requiring dedicated resources
interpretation.0.8–1.0: Near-impenetrable — not recommended without exceptional strategic rationale

negative_variables.name: capital_intensity
negative_variables.definition: Capital required to launch and sustain the adjacency, relative to the company's current capacity. Higher values reduce the adjacency score.

interpretation.0.0–0.19: Minimal capital — can be funded from operations
interpretation.0.2–0.39: Low capital — modest investment, quick payback
interpretation.0.4–0.59: Moderate capital — meaningful but manageable investment
interpretation.0.6–0.79: High capital — significant balance sheet commitment
interpretation.0.8–1.0: Very high capital — requires external funding or major reallocation

negative_variables.name: time_to_viability
negative_variables.definition: Time required to reach first meaningful revenue. Higher values indicate longer runways and reduce the adjacency score.

interpretation.0.0–0.19: Immediate viability — revenue possible within 30 days

negative_variables.name: risk_exposure
negative_variables.definition: Legal, operational, financial, or reputational downside if the adjacency fails or underperforms. Higher values reduce the adjacency score.

interpretation.0.0–0.19: Minimal downside — failure is low-cost and reversible
interpretation.0.4–0.59: Moderate risk — meaningful but recoverable exposure
interpretation.0.6–0.79: High risk — significant downside requiring mitigation
interpretation.0.8–1.0: Very high risk — existential or irreversible exposure

weight_validation.note: Positive weights sum to 0.83. Negative weights sum to -0.33. Net maximum score approaches 1.0 for ideal adjacencies with zero friction.

score_interpretation.0.76–1.00: Top adjacency — high conviction expansion pathway
score_interpretation.0.63–0.75: Strong adjacency — viable with strategic investment
score_interpretation.0.50–0.62: Moderate adjacency — possible but not priority
score_interpretation.0.35–0.49: Weak adjacency — resource intensive, low ROI
